To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activation of CRHR1 in HT22 cells triggers neuritogenesis by an atypical soluble adenosine 3′,5′-monophosphate (cAMP)-dependent, ERK1 /2-independent pathway.
CRH triggers neurite outgrowth and growth arrest in hippocampal HT22-CRFR1 cells by a cAMP-dependent mechanism that is mediated by sAC and ERK1/ 2 independent.
(1) CRH induces neuronal differentiation by a sAC-cAMP-dependent, ERK-independent mechanism, and (2) sAC and tmACs are involved in CRH-induced c-fos and CREB expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of cAMP-dependent cell differentiation in hippocampal HT22 cells, which is triggered by the activation of CRHR1.
the mechanisms underlying the CRHR1-mediated cAMP signalling pathways in the central nervous system, and how they are involved in cell growth and differentiation.
the elucidation of the mechanisms involved in CRH-mediated neuritogenesis, which may be of importance for the understanding of the role played by CRH in the development of the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CRHR1 activates both tmACs and the atypical sAC, but only sACh-derived cAMP is required for CRH-triggered neuritogenesis.

the activation of CRHR1 by CRH in HT22-C cells leads to the activation of both tmACs and the atypical sAC, which in turn leads to the phosphorylation of CREB and c-fos transcription, and the induction of cell differentiation.
the activation of GPCRs triggers the engagement of both cAMP sources in a cell-type specific manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

sAC-dependent cAMP signalling is required for the neuritogenesis induced by CRHR1 activation, while tmAC-dependent signalling is necessary for the cAMP-dependent phosphorylation of CREB and c-fos transcription.
CRHR1-mediated sAC activity is required for cAMP-dependent neuritogenesis in hippocampal cells.
sAC-dependent, tmAC-independent signalling pathways are involved in the neurite outgrowth triggered by activated CRH receptor 1 in hippocampalian neuronal cells.

the cAMP microdomains generated downstream of GPCR activation can be used to regulate specific signalling pathways, which may be exploited in the future for therapeutic interventions.
